why: the kit's own chain is the look reference, the cheapest of the lot and passes every gate; nothing tested beats it
as a replacement for the kit's bloom and DoF it needs two custom effects and per-version re-tuning to get back to the kit's look, and it is not cheaper
reaches near parity only with custom effects on top, so it buys nothing over the kit's chain
diagnostic variant: shows the DoF effect is what softens text
SMAA is 3.5x cheaper than the 4-subframe jitter but loses soft shadows and motion blur as well as edge quality
edge quality is fine with MSAA 4, but a single sample drops the soft shadow and the motion blur that the kit's jitter gives for about 3x the time
native tone mappers fight the kit's hex-faithful grade
superseded by A4, where the same LUT sits on the kit's own chain
same look as the kit at a higher time per frame (BokehPass re-renders the scene for depth) with softer silhouettes and no new capability
same loss as the pp SMAA variant, with more aliasing
do not bump three now: drift is far below the 40 dB bar and nothing in r186 improves our plates
a bump is a one-off re-grade (+7.3 % exposure, retire patchShadows) plus re-verifying every shipped spot, for no gain
conditional variant (drift was not negligible), run as a probe: shows pp minor versions change semantics silently

verdict: ADOPT-FOR per-spot LUT grade or a one-off tail effect
why: 14 added lines, no change to the kit's output when off, seek-safe, one 0.6 MB ESM dependency

package: three + postprocessing (pmndrs, no React, no bundler)
verdict: ADOPT-FOR single-sample plates and quick previews with pmndrs effects
why: Passes G1-G4 with the kit builders unmodified, 11 ms a frame, no bundler, 53 lines of variant code; needs two shader-chunk patches (kit shadows, 21-line Neutral tone map for three r160) and DoF-before-bloom ordering.

R3F reproduces the vanilla frame to the last bit and passes every gate, but costs 6x the installed deps, a bundler, 2.4x the variant code and about ten seek hazards, with no pixel, speed or capability gain.

verdict: ADOPT-FOR cherry-pick (port without React) SoftShadows and MeshReflectorMaterial into the kit
why: Most helpers duplicate the kit or three/addons, and Float, Sparkles, AccumulativeShadows and MeshTransmissionMaterial fail G3 or worse (Math.random, clocks, history); only two ideas are worth porting.

Redundant with pmndrs postprocessing used directly (same pixels); inside R3F it builds its pipeline over several async cycles, hard-codes blend and mask choices, re-creates the composer on camera swap and warns without a lights prop; keep only if R3F itself is adopted.

verdict: ADOPT-FOR multi-body physical motion (scatter, pile, topple, drop onto things), baked at build time; keep springs for single-object moves
why: A baked table is a pure function of t, so the real kit page passes G1-G3 bit-exactly and G4 cleanly for a 0.13 s bake and a 387 KB table, while naive live physics fails G2 and even the seekable live variant needs a replay per rewind plus 114 MB of tooling.

why: Passes G1-G3 and matches the DOM baseline to 51-56 dB on all 120 frames, but costs a Vite build, about 106 MB of deps, 254 scene lines against 65, three hand-written workarounds (cubic-bezier easing, text/unit splitting, exact spring) plus a parametric Bezier and font-wait, a lossy video hand-off into HyperFrames (GOP and BT.709 gotchas, 35 dB after re-encode), and upstream has had no code commit since 2025-02-16 (last stable 3.17.2 on 2024-12-14, vite capped at 5); only reconsider as ADOPT-FOR generator-timeline explainer scenes with a live editor if manimgx and HyperFrames+GSAP prove insufficient.

licence: Remotion License (source-available): Free License for individuals, for-profit orgs up to 3 employees, non-profits and evaluation; paid Company License (remotion.pro) otherwise

package: pack type/ease.js + type/presets.js (own code, no library)
why: Lowest-risk engine and the correctness reference; stays as the component layer (type, gfx, captions) while GSAP is used for authoring.

repo: lottie-web (baseline that dotLottie Web is compared against)
why: Default Lottie player for HyperFrames: works through the native adapter with 3 lines; its only gate miss is G2 at 84.9 dB (1 to 3 pixels on a 22 %-alpha hairline at frames 6, 10, 11), i.e. Chrome SVG raster noise of the same class that makes the inline-SVG draw-on render byte-different at -w 1 vs -w 2.

Same speed as the SVG renderer, strictly fewer features, and it renders a BLANK video in HyperFrames unless its container has an explicit pixel size (HyperFrames stamps the root size after inline scripts run).

The integration the HyperFrames docs describe (register the player on window.__hfLottie) renders blank for current dotlottie-web; use the hf-seek bridge instead.
Passes all three gates headless under ANGLE-Metal but adds a GPU raster dependency for no visible gain; the software build is bit-stable and fast enough. Not rendered through HyperFrames.

Not enough: convertPathData(makeArcs) also has to go (ablation of all 33 preset plugins).

Eight times the code of the HTML route for the same picture; every CSS behaviour (wrap, tracking, kerning, clipping, shadows) is re-implemented by hand.
Wins H.264 quality per byte at both rates (+1.0 dB / +0.6 VMAF at 4.6 MB, +2.5 dB / +3.3 VMAF at 1.34 MB over Mediabunny at equal size), speed is not a constraint for upload copies.
1.7 dB worse than the two-pass recipe at the same size for 3 s instead of 21 s; nothing to gain over Mediabunny's browser encoders either.
Duplicates Mediabunny's hardware path with a bigger file and lower quality than x264.

package: cbirds (live terminal mode, captured from a pseudo-terminal with --snapshot)
why: The live loop steps on CLOCK_MONOTONIC: three runs with the same --seed 5 --frames 120 gave three different snapshots (27.7-28.0 dB), so screen-recording cbirds in a terminal can never be frame-exact; use --record.

Byte-identical GIF twice and on the never-run tarball build's first run, and prefix-stable (a 4 s take is the first 133 frames of the 9 s take); G2 fails for the raw simulation because frame N exists only after simulating 0..N-1, which baking fixes.

package: cbirds --record GIF --render braille (cells painted as a terminal shows them)
why: Same gates as E1 and the only mode that looks like a real terminal; 7 colours of 2x4-dot cells at 1080x1920, so fine dots may shimmer after platform re-encodes (not tested).

package: cbirds --record GIF --say TEXT (the flock writes a word and holds it)
verdict: ADOPT-FOR 'flock writes a word' title stings, baked
why: The word forms within about 2 s and holds while the rest of the flock orbits it; strokes are made of birds, so it reads as a playful dot-matrix title rather than typography, and the default size is modest (about a third of a 16:9 width).

verdict: ADOPT-FOR murmuration b-roll and transition plates, baked
why: The most cinematic mode (depth, dusk ramp, banking) and as deterministic as E1 on one build; it differs from frame 0 across builds (240 warm-up steps run before the first frame), so the baked MP4 and its SHA-256, not the command, is the artifact.

Frame lines are identical run to run and it steps at exactly 1/30 s, but the header carries time(NULL) (bytes differ every run) and turning a cast into pixels needs a third-party terminal renderer; the GIF path already paints braille itself.

package: cbirds --record GIF --text FILE (the letters of a text take flight and land)
verdict: ADOPT-FOR 'code that flies' b-roll from our own text, baked
why: Letters lift off in a wave, flock and land on their own cells, deterministic like E1; a 5x7 bitmap font in 12x20 cells gives 90 columns at 1080 px wide, small on a phone, and a whole cycle runs 34 s.

package: terminal/bake-plate.sh (cbirds -O2 -ffp-contract=off -> GIF -> 30 fps H.264) as a HyperFrames 0.8.142 <video> layer
verdict: ADOPT-FOR terminal/flock b-roll plates and 'flock writes a word' titles, baked at build time into a 30 fps MP4 played as a video layer
why: Two bakes gave byte-identical GIF and MP4 (x264 on one thread); every recorded frame maps to exactly one plate frame (300 frames, bt709, faststart); a -w 2 HyperFrames render matched the plate 300/300 by frame identity (39.9-41.6 dB, decoder colour path), the same pattern as baked Rapier.

package: cbirds built -O0 / -O3 -ffp-contract=off / x86_64 (Rosetta) vs the default -O3 arm64 build
why: Diagnostic: every build is deterministic on its own, but the chaotic flock diverges between builds (no-FMA arm64 and x86_64 at frame 50, -O0 at frame 158, 3D at frame 0), so pin the build flags and keep the baked MP4 rather than promising re-bakes on other machines.
